guides.title: Render escaped HTML on the server
guides.summary: Use the server entrypoint to turn an HTML template into a string.
guides.markdown:
Import html and renderToString from the public server entrypoint. Interpolate text values into html templates. The renderer escapes text rather than interpreting it as markup.

Do not concatenate untrusted text into HTML source or use unsafe raw-HTML helpers for it. Escaping text does not authorize a request or validate application URLs. Server rendering produces an HTML string. It does not attach browser event handlers or hydrate an application.

guides.title: Select template branches and optional attributes
guides.summary: Render conditional content without building HTML strings.
guides.markdown: Use `when` to select a branch and `choose` to match a value with strict equality. Their callbacks run while the template expression is evaluated. Use `nothing` for an empty child value. `ifDefined(undefined)` omits an attribute; other values, including `null`, `false`, and `0`, are serialized as values. HTML escaping does not validate URL schemes or authorize a destination.

guides.title: Render lists with stable item keys
guides.summary: Use keyed repeat for lists whose DOM items should keep their identity.
guides.markdown: `repeat(items, keyFn, templateFn)` gives the browser renderer a stable key for each item so it can retain matching DOM nodes when the list changes. Server rendering emits the initial ordered markup; it does not prove browser node reuse. Use `join` when you need a renderable separator between values. Plain arrays and `map` are enough when item identity does not matter.

guides.title: Render current form values before hydration
guides.summary: Seed input, checkbox, and textarea values in server-rendered HTML.
guides.markdown: Use `.value=${bind(state, path)}` and `.checked=${bind(state, path)}` to render the current field values. `live(value)` supplies the current value when the renderer reconciles an existing DOM property. On the server these helpers only produce initial markup; client rendering or hydration is required for browser write-back. A binding does not validate submitted data or authorize a server action.

guides.title: Compose component CSS from reviewed values
guides.summary: Use css tagged templates for static styles and reserve unsafeCSS for trusted values.
guides.markdown: `css` accepts numeric interpolations and other `CSSResult` values. It rejects ordinary strings, so use static styles and typed numbers for normal composition. `unsafeCSS` marks a string as trusted CSS; it does not sanitize it. Never pass user input, request data, or other untrusted values to `unsafeCSS`.

guides.title: Compose components with component tags
guides.summary: Write child components as <${Class}> tags; attributes become props and content becomes children.
guides.markdown:
Write a child component as a component tag: bind its class in tag position, `<${Card} padding="sm">children`, or self-close it, `<${Icon} entry=${ArrowIcon} />`. The closing tag binds the same class; another class is an error. Attributes become `props` the way `component()` takes them: `name="text"` passes the string (character references decoded), a bare `name` passes `true`, `name=${value}` passes the value as is, `name="a ${b}"` passes text, and `.prop=${v}`, `?bool=${v}` and `@event=${f}` keep their prefix in the prop key. `...=${props}` spreads an object; later attributes override earlier ones. Prop names keep their case, so `rowCount=${12}` sets `rowCount`. Children become `children`: nothing for empty or whitespace content, the text for plain text, the value itself for one binding, and a template otherwise. Named slots are props with template values: ``footer=${html`

Saved

`}``. `html` compiles each tag into the result `component()` returns, so SSR, hydration, drafts and service scopes behave the same. Use tags for markup. Keep `component(Class, props, children)` only where the class is chosen at runtime, such as from a registry; `cossack check templates --verbose` hints at `component()` calls with a literal class. Template holes are not contextually typed. Annotate callback parameters, such as `onValueChange=${(value: string) => ...}`, and write object and array literals with `satisfies`, such as `state=${{ page: 1 } satisfies TableState}`, so literal types are kept. The template check reports a prop the component does not declare, a value of the wrong type, a missing required prop, and a static text value for a non-string prop (`count="3"`; write `count=${3}`).

guides.title: Use the binding forms the template check accepts
guides.summary: Know what each binding form does and which template problems fail the check and the build.
guides.markdown:
An `html` or `svg` template has five binding forms. In child content, `${value}` renders text, a template, a list or a component. In a tag, `name=${value}` sets an attribute (`null`, `undefined` or `nothing` removes it; `ifDefined()` removes it only for undefined), `name="a ${b}"` interpolates text, `.prop=${value}` sets a DOM property, `?name=${boolean}` toggles a boolean attribute, `@event=${handler}` adds a listener, and `...=${object}` spreads attributes, properties and listeners. A `.`, `?` or `@` binding takes one whole value. A component tag binds a class in tag position.

Run `cossack check templates` (or rely on the Vite build) after editing templates. It reads every template with the project's TypeScript program and reports each problem with file, line and column. Errors fail the check and the build; warnings do not. Structural errors: unclosed or mismatched elements, `<div />` on an HTML element (only void and SVG elements self-close), a binding that renders nothing (inside a comment, `<div ${x}>`, or interrupting an attribute name), an unknown binding prefix such as `:value=`, a prefixed attribute without a binding (`@click="save()"`), a component tag that never closes or closes with another class, and a template literal with markup but no `html` tag in child content, which renders as escaped text. Type errors: an attribute the element does not have (custom elements accept global attributes, with a warning for others), an attribute value of the wrong type (static enumerated values are checked too), an inline `onclick` attribute, an `@event` handler that does not accept the element's event, a `?attr` value that is not boolean, an unknown or read-only `.prop`, and component tag props. Attribute types come from `@cossackframework/renderer/attributes`.

`parseTemplate` from `@cossackframework/renderer/template` returns the same element tree and structural problems the check uses.
